title: The Fire That Rebuilt London
objective: Explain in under a minute what the Great Fire of London was, how big the loss was, what is still uncertain, and how the rebuilding changed the city.
audience: General viewers curious about history; no prior knowledge assumed.

message.core_message: A fire that began in one bakery destroyed much of the old city, and the way London was rebuilt, in brick and stone, was a direct answer to it.
key_points: It began just after midnight on Sunday 2 September 1666 at a bakery on Pudding Lane
Estimated 13,200-13,500 houses, 86-87 parish churches and St Paul's were destroyed
The death toll is disputed (traditionally six)
Rebuilding required brick and stone; Wren rebuilt St Paul's; the Monument is 202 ft

avoid: a single death toll stated as fact
HUD labels and counters with no purpose

constraints: Every number on screen carries its uncertainty where the sources give a range
No generated imagery is presented as archival or as a real photograph

references.description: Workspace technique records for paper-cut title sequences and archival collage (catalogue/data/references/cut-paper-title-sequence.json, archival-mono-collage.json)

audio.notes: Warm, low music bed; paper and stamp foley under the voice.

research.reason: Historical claims with figures: houses, churches, dates, deaths.

creative_directions.name: Editorial paper collage
creative_directions.concept: Each beat is a poster assembled in front of the viewer from torn paper, tape, halftone and ink-cut figures on kraft. Time passes as stamped day-tickets; scale is a counter on a torn sheet; the quiet beat about deaths is a single typed line and a paper '6'. The rebuilding is bricks stacking into a skyline.

visual_identity.palette: kraft cream, ink charcoal, vermilion, marigold, slate blue
visual_identity.typography: Archivo Black display, Nunito text, Space Mono for dates
visual_identity.texture: procedural paper grain, halftone, torn edges

motion_language.transitions: push-over, torn-sheet wipe, dissolve on a single object, match-cut circle to dome

composition.approach: asymmetric stacks, one dominant cut-out per beat

creative_directions.why_it_fits: Tactile materials match a story about wood, paper and brick; the style stays warm for a grave subject without sensationalism.

creative_directions.name: Archival document table
creative_directions.concept: A slow camera over documents, maps and press-style clippings on an aged table.
creative_directions.why_it_fits: Authentic for history, but depends on real period imagery that this workspace cannot source offline.

success_criteria: Every on-screen figure matches the dossier
Visible change at least every 3 s while narration speaks (except declared stillness)
No two consecutive scenes share a composition
Ends smaller and quieter than it begins
